title: Cystoscopy
what: A urologist looks inside your bladder with a thin tube with a camera. It goes in through the urethra, the tube you pee through.
why: For blood in the urine, frequent infections, problems peeing, or for a check-up after bladder treatment.
duration: usually 5 to 15 minutes; about 30 minutes with preparation
tell_doctor: Blood thinners. The doctor decides what to do with them
Allergies to medicines or numbing gels
If you have burning or a fever now. An infection is usually treated first

prepare.title: Urine test
prepare.text: Sometimes you are asked to do a urine test beforehand, to rule out an infection.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: With local numbing, you can usually eat and drink. With general anesthesia, do not eat, following your clinic's rules.

prepare.title: Toilet
prepare.text: Empty your bladder before the procedure.

bring: Urine test and ultrasound results, if you have them
steps: You undress below the waist and lie on a chair or couch
The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
A numbing gel is put into the urethra, and you wait a few minutes
The doctor gently puts in the thin tube with a camera
The bladder is filled with sterile water, and its walls are checked
If needed, a tiny piece of tissue is taken for testing
feel: It feels unpleasant and unusual, but usually bearable
As the bladder fills, you feel the need to pee. This is normal
If it hurts, tell the doctor
after: For 1 to 2 days, peeing may sting a little
Your urine may look pinkish. This can happen
Drink more water in the first few days
The doctor usually tells you what they saw right away. Tissue results come later
red_flags: A fever over 38 degrees, or chills
You cannot pee, or there is bright blood with clots
Strong pain in the lower belly

faq.a: Usually not. A numbing gel and a thin, flexible tube are used. It is unpleasant, but bearable.

faq.q: Can I go home right after a cystoscopy?
faq.a: Yes, if it was done with local numbing. After general anesthesia, you need someone to take you home.

reminders.text: Cystoscopy soon. Bring your referral and test results. Use the toilet before the procedure.
